markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Normal (>99%)** · Confident · Careful review
Single-class conformal set, but the second model (MUSK) picks a different top class [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Normal >99%, Benign <1% | Sharply peaked |
| Conformal set | {Normal} at α=0.1 | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.99 / 1.0 | No input flag |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Different top class | Independent check disagrees |
| Similar cases | 4 of 5 Normal | Mostly supportive |

## Tissue evidence
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 0, 1, 2) · ↓ invasive · Strong tubule score; linked to non-invasive · Validated
- **Tumor-infiltrating stroma** (region 1) · ↓ invasive · Score below typical, lowering invasive association [F4] · Validated
- **Dense lymphocytic infiltrate** (regions 1, 4) · context · Above-typical TILs; descriptive only · Weak
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (region 7) · ↓ invasive · Present; linked to lower invasive likelihood · Validated

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI includes 0 (−0.005 to 0.007); not shown to reflect the classifier. Mitoses (0/20) is Unreliable and contributes here.

## Could be wrong if
- The image is JPEG-degraded (simulated, severity 3), which may shift model output.
- One similar reference case is InSitu (BACH_0300), and the second model disagrees.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 1, 4**: Confirm the lymphocytic infiltrate is real; its spot check was only 8/20.
2. **Regions 0, 1, 2**: Check that glands look benign, not invasive architecture.
3. **Regions 6, 11**: Highest regional invasive probability (7%, 5%); confirm benign.
